title: IS12:: printing1.c (2.1)

lines.explanation: This line is required since we are using printf
Empty lines make a program more readable
When the program is called, function main will be executed. Every program should have function main. void indicates that main does not return a value.
This printf statement will print Hello, World! and move printing cursor to the beginning of next line

Two integer values will be printed there. First one (10) will occupy exactly 5 output positions as specified by %5d. Second will  occupy  8 positions as specified by %8d. Since 10 and 99 themselves occupy  2 positions each, leading blanks are printed

This printf statements will print two floating point values - one will be printed as 3.14 thus occupying as requested 4 positions in total with 2 after point and another as  0.00100 occupying all 8 requested positions with 5 digits after the point
The %c specification is for printing characters. In this case the program will print: Here are characters A G  Note that 'A' and '@' are literal constants and have to be in single quotes.
